decision_rule.D1: reachability is E272's published contract (flip inside the tail's published multiplier range), imported from e272, not copied
decision_rule.D2: the branch is E279's deflation: a stranded tail reaches while the substitute does not; only rows carrying a degenerate range are candidates
decision_rule.D3: a row needs relative tolerance tau_r = gap_pct_r / 100, so the band is [min tau_r, +infinity); reachable at the published tolerance iff min tau_r <= TOL/100
decision_rule.D4: the band is only a tolerance if the instrument still discriminates inside it: at the band's lower end the same test is applied to every reading and a share >= 0.5 counts as a collapse
decision_rule.D5: no reburn: published faces re-read only, no draw, no band rebuilt, no engine
decision_rule.D6: scope is measured; <slug>_latest mirrors are dropped by name and the drop is published

no_bill: measurement only: E272's published per-row tail ranges and E279's stranded census are re-read. No draw stream is drawn, no band rebuilt, no engine runs. A verdict here is a statement about the published numbers, not about the market.

title: a degenerate tail can only reach a row when the flip equals its single multiplier -- does that ever happen, and how loose a tolerance would it take?

tolerance_band.statement: the branch becomes reachable only at a relative tolerance of at least 63.0256 pct (0.6303 of the flip); every looser test fires it

verdict_reason: 0 of 2 candidate readings reach at the published tolerance; the nearest needs a relative tolerance of 63.0256 pct (a flip 2.705x its degenerate value), and at that tolerance 21 of 24 published tail readings -- 87.5 pct, against 2 published -- would read reachable, so the test that fires the branch is not the test that published the family.
